program.checker_template: Execute exactly the supplied visual check on the source and edited images. Follow its saved binding, criteria and dependency evidence. Do not invent edits or infer an expected overall answer. Return JSON status, concise image-grounded evidence, and confidence (a number from 0 to 1, or null if unavailable). Confidence is your reported confidence in this check's observation, not a calibrated probability. A requested fulfillment check uses complete/partial/absent/unknown. A support check uses pass/fail/unknown. A known negative supporting observation can inform a requested check; it is not automatically uncertainty. Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish the requested fact. Do not count supporting facts as completed edits. Assess only the supplied check, not the overall instruction label.

n1: The node’s criterion only checks whether the mug ends up right of the headphones, so it treats a completed relocation as complete even when the edited image also retains an extra mug at the original location. The source has one mug left of the headphones; the edit appears to leave a blurred mug-shaped remnant there while adding a mug on the right. Make the decision explicitly compare source and edited images and assess both requested progress and whether the original mug was actually moved rather than duplicated/left behind; distinguish that case from a clean relocation. Preserve an unknown outcome if the remnant or object identity cannot be judged reliably. The five high-confidence, identical traces show a systematic criterion/binding gap, not transport or dependency failure; the reference ‘partial’ constrains the aggregate but does not by itself establish the remnant as ground truth.
